lesson_title: A War That Was Cold, and Hot
hook_text: For forty years, the two most powerful countries on Earth were enemies. They never fought a battle against each other. Why not?
clip_script: 1945. Two giants stand above the rest: the United States and the Soviet Union. Superpowers. They want opposite worlds. And each has the bomb. If one attacks, the other strikes back, and both are destroyed. So they never fight directly. Instead, they build alliances: NATO, then the Warsaw Pact. They fill the airwaves with propaganda. They send spies. They race to build bigger bombs and to reach space first. And they fight through others. In Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan, superpower weapons kill millions. In Angola, Soviet and Cuban support meets American and South African support, and the war lasts for decades. Here at home, the apartheid government calls every opponent a communist. It was called the Cold War. For the people caught in the middle, it was anything but cold.
visual_style: Two giant chess pieces facing each other across a world map; a NATO and a Warsaw Pact flag on either side of a line through Europe; a radio tower broadcasting; a map of Africa with Angola highlighted and arrows from different directions.
pacing: Steady build through the methods, a sharp final line.
